dedup_removal_2026-08-09.finding: process_branded.py's Step 5 dedup-by-description was silently discarding ~1.39M legitimate distinct products (different UPCs/retailers sharing identical description text) - these were already live/searchable in Qdrant regardless, since dedup only ever applied to the JSON pipeline, never to what got embedded
dedup_removal_2026-08-09.action: removed dedup step from process_branded.py entirely
dedup_removal_2026-08-09.result: branded_clean.json grew from 461,022 -> 1,849,223 records. Remaining ~150k gap vs Qdrant's 1,999,864 branded_foods points fully accounted for by non-US market (~13k) + missing-calorie-data (~137k) filters, confirmed via direct math, not a mystery

duplicate_point_bug_2026-08-09.finding: backfill_nutrition_to_qdrant.py's resolve_point_ids used limit=len(batch) with a dict-based id_map - when a qdrant_id had 2+ duplicate Qdrant points, scroll would fill the batch limit with duplicate copies and silently drop other requested IDs entirely (fake ~28% not-found rate in first TEST_MODE run)
duplicate_point_bug_2026-08-09.fix: over-fetch (3x) + paginate until all requested IDs resolved; write payload to every duplicate point, not just one; count not-found by unique fdc_id
duplicate_point_bug_2026-08-09.scope_confirmed_via_full_census: only 50 branded_foods qdrant_ids have duplicates (all exactly 2 copies, 100 points total) out of 1,999,864 - a contiguous early block, not fleet-wide
duplicate_point_bug_2026-08-09.allergen_safety_check: IMPORTANT - checked whether extract_allergens_to_qdrant.py's same dict-based pattern silently under-wrote allergen data on these 50 duplicate-point records. Full census (not sample): 50/50 duplicate groups have IDENTICAL allergen payloads across both copies, 0 mismatches, 0 branded_foods points anywhere with missing/invalid milk field. Allergen data confirmed safe and consistent - no user-facing safety issue.
duplicate_point_bug_2026-08-09.followup_not_urgent: 50 branded_foods records still exist as duplicate points (2x each) - cosmetic/search-quality issue (could show up twice in results), not a safety issue. Dedupe to 1 point per qdrant_id is the clean long-term fix, low priority.

provenance_tagging_2026-08-09.vitamin_a: Do NOT auto-convert IU to RAE with a flat factor - explicitly investigated and rejected in original MAIN2 session (FDA's real conversion has 3 different factors depending on source: 0.3 retinol, 0.6 supplemental beta-carotene, 1.2 other carotenoids - USDA data doesn't indicate source, so any flat factor is wrong for a meaningful share of records). Correct pattern: RAE present -> vitamin_a_rae_mcg + vitamin_a_source:'measured_rae'. Only IU present -> vitamin_a_rae_mcg=null, vitamin_a_source:'unsupported_conversion'. Neither -> both null, vitamin_a_source:'no_data'
provenance_tagging_2026-08-09.folate: folate_dfe_mcg preferred (1190), Total (1177) as fallback. folate_source: 'measured_dfe' | 'fallback_from_total' | 'no_data'
provenance_tagging_2026-08-09.vitamin_d_GAP_FOUND: MAIN2 built and tested a Vitamin D mcg normalization module (nutrient_normalization.py, fixed 1:40 IU-to-mcg ratio, verified against FDA's own published example 800 IU -> 20 mcg) but NEVER integrated it into any processor script. process_branded.py as of tonight only reads ID 1114 (direct mcg) with no fallback to 1110 (IU). Being fixed as part of tonight's Cursor task: vitamin_d_mcg + vitamin_d_source: 'measured_mcg' | 'converted_from_iu' | 'no_data'
provenance_tagging_2026-08-09.fndds_additional_description_GAP_FOUND: MAIN2 investigated food_attribute.csv and found FNDDS's 'Additional Description' attribute type (9,647 rows) contains alternate/translated names (Spanish translations like 'leche fresca', clarifying notes) - resolved as worth capturing for voice-search matching on non-English names, but never implemented. SR Legacy's equivalent (type 'Common Name', 1,074 rows) was explicitly resolved as low-value/skip. Being fixed as part of tonight's Cursor task: new field in fndds_clean.json (e.g. additional_description)
provenance_tagging_2026-08-09.sugar_NUTRIENT_ID_BUG_FOUND: CRITICAL - process_branded.py maps nutrient_id 1063 to 'sugar', but per MAIN2's real coverage audit, ID 1063 ('Sugars, Total') has only 698 branded records with data - essentially unused. Correct modern ID is 2000 ('Total Sugars'), with 1,790,107 branded records and 6,007 SR Legacy records. Sugar has likely been silently null for ~99.96% of branded foods this whole time. Cross-checked every other ID in the 39-field schema against the same audit - no other mismatches found, appears isolated to sugar. Being fixed as part of tonight's Cursor task.
provenance_tagging_2026-08-09.missing_trace_minerals_FOUND: Iodine (1100), Chromium (1096), Molybdenum (1102) were explicitly approved for inclusion in MAIN2's 'expand nutrient capture, simple mapping' decision but never added to the schema. Chlorine (1088) and Biotin (1176) discussed in the same category but not explicitly named in the final decision - lower confidence, include for consistency. Being added as part of tonight's Cursor task.

nutrition_payload_backfill.fndds_dietary_tags_unresolved_LOW_PRIORI: MAIN2 planned (8/2) to sample 500 random FNDDS descriptions for dietary keywords (vegan/gluten-free/etc.) to decide if a full dietary-tag scan was worth building for FNDDS - this sample check was never actually run. FNDDS currently has 0 dietary tags in Qdrant. Reasoning for likely-fine-as-is: FNDDS descriptions are standardized USDA reference text ('Milk, whole'), not marketing copy, so dietary claims are unlikely to appear - but this was never empirically confirmed like the original plan intended. Not blocking, revisit if it ever seems to matter.

app_integration_followups_SEPARATE_FROM_.dietary_preferences_wiring: lookup_food() in nutrition_service.py expects the caller to pass dietary_preferences in as a param - it does NOT fetch it from Mongo itself. Whatever calls this function (a route handler) needs a small update to fetch the user's UserProfile.dietary_preferences and pass it through. This wiring was never completed - without it, dietary/allergen filtering isn't actually active end-to-end even though the underlying filter logic exists.
app_integration_followups_SEPARATE_FROM_.patch_food_log_allergy_block_gap: CONFIRMED via session's own PR description (authoritative 'known open items' list): PATCH /food/{log_id} has no explicit handling for an edit that trips a severe allergy block. The equivalent gap in the primary create path (POST /food, log_food()) was found and fixed this session, but the edit/PATCH path was never given the same treatment. Risk: editing an existing food log to trigger a severe allergy match could silently succeed with bad data (calories: None) instead of being blocked, same failure mode already fixed for the create path.
